hello.speaker: sister
hello.text: Mara rang the ferry bell once for the living and twice for the dead. When the collectors came, they took the boat, the bell, then her. Seris was there. I will not pretend a rescue can make that memory clean.

choices.text: Ask for the memory that can identify her soul.
Listen to the story of the ferry.

memory.speaker: sister
memory.text: She hated deep water. Everyone thought a ferryman must love it. She crossed because people needed crossing. Tell her I remember the courage, not the fear.

bell.speaker: sister
bell.text: The raiders left it in the ruined boathouse. Bring it back because it is ours, not because it will buy my forgiveness.

returned.speaker: sister
returned.text: You brought it back. Keep it until Mara is free; let it call her by her own name. When she comes home, she can hang it herself.

history.speaker: sister
history.text: The river used to mark the edge of the archlord’s grant. His agents could collect a toll at the bridge, never at the ferry. When the bridge fell, they quietly began calling every crossing a bridge. Mara kept the old maps. They called that defiance. She called it knowing where she lived. The map in the manor still shows the original boundary.
